title: Ethernet is named after the ether.
description:
Ethernet is named after the ether. Luminiferous ether was the 19th century idea of a medium that carried light.

Wrote the memo to Xerox PARC management explaining how Ethernet would work. It is dated 22 May.

He did not call it coax-net. The first network ran at 2.94 Mbit/s over shared coaxial cable at Xerox PARC.

The ether could be anything. Metcalfe: coax, twisted pair, radio, optical fibre, power line, whatever you wanted.

The reach of the 1983 standard for 10 Mbit/s Ethernet over coaxial cable.

He named it for the medium, not the cable.

Sources:
- https://www.eng.hawaii.edu/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/Looking-Back-on-40-Years-of-Ethernet.pdf (read): places Metcalfe's memo to PARC management on 22 May 1973; he chose the name from the 19th century phrase "Ether", luminiferous ether being the medium through which light was thought to travel; the team used thick coaxial cable because it could be tapped passively; Metcalfe: "we didn't call it coax-net" and the ether "could be coax, twisted pair, radio, optical fibers, power line, whatever you wanted".
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethernet (read): name drawn from the old idea of luminiferous aether and meant to stress that Ethernet could run over any medium; first network ran at 2.94 Mbit/s over shared coaxial cable at Xerox PARC; a 1983 standard covered 10 Mbit/s over coaxial cable up to 500 metres (10BASE5); the DIX Blue Book followed in 1980.
